Sciatic nerve pain, often called sciatica, is a condition where pain radiates along the path of the sciatic nerve. This nerve runs from the lower back down through the hips, buttocks, and each leg. Pain can vary from a mild ache to a sharp, burning sensation, or even a feeling like an electric shock. Sciatica can be caused by a herniated disc, bone spurs, or spinal narrowing that compresses the nerve. Symptoms often include lower back pain, numbness, tingling, and weakness in the legs. Effective treatments include physical therapy, stretching, medications, and in some cases, surgery. Early intervention can help manage pain and prevent it from becoming chronic.

Pericardial effusion is the buildup of too much fluid in the double-layered, saclike structure around the heart (pericardium).

The space between these layers typically contains a thin layer of fluid. But if the pericardium is diseased or injured, the resulting inflammation can lead to excess fluid. Fluid can also build up around the heart without inflammation, such as from bleeding, related to a cancer or after chest trauma.

Pericardial effusion can put pressure on the heart, affecting how the heart works. If untreated, it may lead to heart failure or death in extreme cases.
